---
title: "squirrels"
---

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)
library(cowsay)
set.seed(42)


trials <- sample(c("Success", "Fail"), replace=TRUE, prob = c(0.3, 0.7), size=150)
n_successes <- sum(trials == "Success")
say(paste0("I succeeded ", n_successes, " times"), by="squirrel")


```

```{r}


combined_successes <- c()
for (i in 1:1000) {
  trials <- sample(c("SUCCESS", "FAILURE"),
    size = 150,
    replace = TRUE,
    prob = c(0.3, 0.7)
  )
  #N successes per individual squirrel trialling 150 nuts
  n_successes <- sum(trials == "SUCCESS")
  #A growing vector showing the outcome of each of the 1000 squirrels' trials
  combined_successes <- c(combined_successes, n_successes)
}

df_squirrels <- tibble("N_Successful_Heists" = combined_successes)
ggplot(
  df_squirrels,
  aes(
    x = N_Successful_Heists
  ) 
) +
  geom_bar() + 
  ggtitle("Number of successful heists per squirrel (simulated)")

```


Plotting a binomial dist

```{r}
#Want to plot X~B(150, 0.3) - same as our data before
#Have to do by hand by calculating each (PX=x) and graphinh

calculated_bdist <- c()
x_values <- c()

for (i in 1:150) {
  prob <- dbinom(i, 150, 0.3)
  x_values <- c(x_values, i)
  calculated_bdist <- c(calculated_bdist, prob)
}
bdist <- tibble("x" = x_values, "p" = calculated_bdist)

ggplot(
  bdist,
  aes(
    x = x,
    y = p
  )
) +
  geom_col() +
  ggtitle("Binomial distribution for n=150, p=0.3")

```
